Subject: Post-call recap — concurrency & rate limits (Acme)

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the performance / SLO questions we discussed:

1) Requirements you stated on the call
- Peak concurrent active requests: 1,200 (short spikes up to 1,500 for marketing events)
- Baseline sustained concurrency: 500
- Sustained throughput target: ~50 requests/sec (avg) for the main chat flow
- Average response size: ~80 tokens (mostly short assistant replies)
- Streaming required: yes — partial token streaming for UI latency, p95 token arrival latency target ~150ms
- Connection model: long-lived client connections with pooling; you prefer HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible.

2) What we discussed from Redwood’s side
- Concurrency = simultaneous in-flight requests handled by the runtime (not TCP connections). For streaming, each in-flight request holds a worker slot until the stream completes or the response is finalized.
- Default hosted plan concurrency cap: 100 concurrent requests. For your scale we should look at either a Dedicated pool or a quota amendment for hosted to reach the numbers above.
- Suggested approach: start with a reserved Dedicated pool of 800 concurrency with burst capacity to 1,500 for peak events, plus a small hosted fallback for non-critical traffic. This keeps steady-state economics reasonable and gives headroom for spikes.
- Token throughput estimate: 50 req/s * 80 tokens = 4,000 tokens/s (~240k tokens/min). This will drive token-rate limits and circuit-breaker sizing.

3) Proposed next steps
- I’ll share a short proposal (attached) that maps concurrency tiers to pricing and SLA options.
- Can you confirm the event spike profile (duration, frequency) — we need that to size burst capacity and retention of KV cache. I attached your traffic forecast CSV you sent earlier and annotated it.
- If you’re comfortable, we can scope a 30-day pilot with a Dedicated pool (800 commit) + burst to 1,500.

4) Questions for you
- Can you confirm whether every client will use HTTP/2 (preferred) or if some will fall back to HTTP/1.1?
- Do you have an expected average open connection TTL per client/session? This affects connection pooling recommendations.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a formal quota/price proposal tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifying items before we sign off on the pilot:

- When you say "concurrency = in-flight requests", does that include requests that are only open to stream partial tokens (i.e., long-lived streaming responses)? For our chat UI some sessions can remain open longer while idle — we want to avoid those holding a worker slot.

- On the token throughput math: the 240k tokens/min number seems high if we assume average messages are shorter during spikes. Can you share the assumptions you used for the 80-token average? We can run a quick sample from our logs if needed.

- Pricing: I’d like the draft proposal to show a committed tier (800) + burst to 1,500, and an explicit hosted fallback rate (e.g., hosted requests billed at pay-as-you-go above the commit). Do you have sample numbers you can share now?

- Pilot: we want a 2-week pilot first (so we can run two scheduled events) before committing to 30 days.

If you can respond to the three bullets above, we’ll sync internally and get back with a go/no-go on the pilot.

Cheers,
Alice

Thanks Alice — quick answers inline below.

> When you say "concurrency = in-flight requests", does that include requests that are only open to stream partial tokens (i.e., long-lived streaming responses)?
Yes — streaming responses hold an in-flight slot while the model is actively producing tokens. Idle open sockets that are not actively streaming (e.g., a client holds an idle HTTP/2 connection with no active request) do NOT count toward concurrency. If you have long-lived sessions that poll frequently but aren’t actively streaming, we recommend a short keepalive + client-side pooling (reuse connections) so sessions don’t create a ton of ephemeral in-flight requests.

> Token throughput assumptions
We used 80 tokens/request as a conservative average for the chat flows you demoed. If your messages trend shorter (30–50 tokens), your token throughput will be proportionally lower. If you can share sample logs for a day (even aggregated histogram of tokens per response), we’ll re-run the math.

> Pricing and pilot length
Attached is an updated draft:
- Committed Dedicated pool (800 concurrency) = pricing_line_item (monthly commit) — see PDF.
- Burst policy: auto-burst to 1,500 for up to 15 minutes per event at 2x the committed unit price for that capacity.
- Hosted fallback: pay-as-you-go at $0.00008 / token for any requests routed to hosted endpoints above committed capacity.
- Pilot: we can do a 2-week pilot (agreed). For pilot compliance we’ll provide elevated support and 2x logging retention for the period.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm pilot dates (2 weeks, include at least one planned event).
2) You share a 24-hour sample of request sizes (or the aggregated histogram).
3) If accepted, we’ll issue a pilot SOW and temporary quota amendment to allow 1,500 burst.

Let me know and I’ll loop in our pricing lead for final numbers (cc’ing Lauren).

Best,
Marissa
